A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InfiniBench with the same research identity, eight skills, and experimental framework. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original evaluations of 13 multimodal models, controlled ablations, judge-reliability analyses, and human verification results in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: V4 retains original model evaluations, ablations, judge comparisons, and human verification outcomes, including Tables 2–10.

M1.justification: The question-generation pipeline, appearance-processing components, redundancy and knowledge filtering, subtitle filtering, and human verification procedures remain unchanged in Section 3.2 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same movie and TV-show sources, eight grounding and reasoning skills, and metadata-only, subtitle-only, and video-plus-subtitle scenarios. Revised sample counts do not establish changed task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The 13 evaluated models and comparator membership within the individual ablations remain unchanged. Table 1 revises descriptive statistics for existing datasets, rather than adding or removing evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Reported benchmark size changes from approximately 91K to 87.7K questions and from 1,219 to 1,217 videos in Table 1, with revised per-skill counts in Figure 3. Split proportions, metrics, and frame budgets remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain whether these are data changes or reporting corrections, or document reruns.

E4.justification: Filtering, modality, frame-count, judge-reliability, and 'I don't know' analyses are retained. Appendix duplicate analysis, human verification, and generation success/failure examples also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 4.4 retains the same Pearson and Spearman correlations, Krippendorff's alpha analyses, and three human ratings per sample on 10% of the test set. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Descriptive dataset results change: Figure 3 reports 27,634 chronological questions instead of 28,611 and 752 spoiler questions instead of 702. Table 1 also revises dataset counts and durations. Model-performance, ablation, and human-verification values in Tables 2–10 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The leaderboard aggregation formula and Appendix B.6 temporal-certificate definition and construction rules are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction and Table 1 caption narrow the largest-QA-set claim from existing benchmarks generally to long and very long video benchmarks. The headline size becomes 87.7K rather than 91K. Claims about the eight skills, model difficulties, memorized knowledge, and multimodal inputs remain stable.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning knowledge leakage, fragmented visual context, modality tradeoffs, and judge reliability remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the transcript-dependence limitation and the same proposed future directions.

D1.justification: Hardware, model configurations, preprocessing and verification instructions, exact generation and judging prompts, project access information, and the unreleased-test-set policy remain unchanged, including the corresponding appendix disclosures.

R1.justification: Table 1 and Sections 2/C.3 revise comparisons with existing datasets. The introduction replaces citations to Regneri 2013, Rohrbach 2014, and three Awad papers with existing MoVQA and TVQA references; those five bibliography entries disappear. Positioning is modestly narrowed toward long-video benchmark scale.

P1.justification: Limited wording and caption edits accompany the revised statistics and qualified size claim, with a paragraph merge in the introduction and small typographic adjustments. The narrative, section order, and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves TVQA from the Long group to Short and adjusts emphasis and its caption. Printed page numbers disappear and text and references reflow. All 23 figures and 10 tables are retained; Figure 3 preserves its chart design with revised numerical labels.

improvement.justification: V4 clarifies the largest-QA claim and aligns MovieChat's Table 1 count with the 14K stated in related work. However, its revised MSRVTT-QA row lists 10K videos averaging 0.25 minutes but 416.6 hours, whereas these figures imply about 41.7 hours. Its 1,217 InfiniBench videos also conflict with the unchanged 923 episodes plus 296 movies in Section 3.3. Unexplained count revisions and these new inconsistencies leave the net effect of clearer positioning and weaker numerical consistency uncertain.
